bendme.headline: Lower your lid. Watch your desktop fold.
bendme.summary: BendMe turns a small movement of your MacBook lid into a live visual effect. Choose a style, start the effect and watch your screen change perspective.
bendme.audience: For MacBook owners who enjoy a playful desktop.
bendme.experienceTitle: Your lid becomes part of the effect
bendme.experience: You gently lower the lid; the desktop bends with it. Open it again to return to the normal view.
bendme.mechanism: A native Swift and Metal renderer uses screen capture and the lid sensor to draw the effect.
bendme.payoff: The effect is the point. It adds a small moment of delight to a familiar machine.
bendme.evidence: BendMe’s public code, built-in artwork renders and the existing MacBook demo are available to inspect.
bendme.barrier: Requires macOS 14+, Apple silicon and a compatible lid sensor. Screen Recording permission is needed. Pause in Appearance or the menu bar.
bendme.demo: Use the supplied lid demo and the two existing shader renders. The video shows physical lid movement; the artwork switch shows the visual states, not live tracking in the website.
bendme.gap: Screen capture stays on the Mac according to the project source. Compatibility should be checked on each supported model; do not promise the global pause shortcut works.
alternatives: A desktop that follows your MacBook lid.
A little lid movement. A visible bend.

resume-ai.headline: Resume AI uses your full experience to help you write for a particular job.
resume-ai.summary: You can’t put everything you’ve done into one resume, but you can keep detailed notes about it. Resume AI is designed to use that unstructured record, the job description and how you want to position yourself to create a relevant draft.
resume-ai.audience: For people whose experience goes beyond what fits in a single resume.
resume-ai.experienceTitle: Keep details that might matter in a later application
resume-ai.experience: Write down what you did within each job and project, without trying to turn it all into resume bullets. Something that seems unrelated today might be useful for another role, and recording it means you don’t have to remember it all later.
resume-ai.mechanism: A job might ask for technical knowledge and communication skills. Relevant examples could come from a science project and a separate call-center job. The idea is for Resume AI to select that context from your notes and use your positioning rationale to guide what the draft emphasizes.
resume-ai.payoff: You don’t have to rely on what you remember or what made it into your last resume.
resume-ai.flowTitle: Use your full experience to write for a particular role
resume-ai.evidence: The example shows how details from different parts of someone’s experience could support one application. It’s an illustration of the intended workflow, not output from a live AI request.
resume-ai.barrier: The draft should use experience you actually recorded. Review what it selects, check the wording and adjust the emphasis before applying. A relevant resume can explain your fit, but it can’t guarantee an interview.
resume-ai.demo: Use the labeled illustration to show detailed notes from a technical project and a customer-support role, followed by a draft for a job asking for both skills. It explains selection across experiences, not verified live generation.
resume-ai.gap: The owner supplied the intended workflow: extensive unstructured experience, job-description matching and positioning rationale. The implementation of storage, selection, rationale controls, export and end-to-end generation still needs verification.
alternatives: Your full experience can inform each application.
Give your next resume more context than your last one.

yabs.headline: YABS Visualizer makes server benchmark results easier to read.
yabs.summary: YABS is a tool that measures server performance. This visualizer presents its results in a format you can look through when comparing virtual private servers, or VPSs.
yabs.audience: For developers comparing VPS benchmark results.
yabs.experienceTitle: Use the measurements to compare servers
yabs.experience: You start with results from YABS and look through the measurements in the visualizer. You can then consider how those results relate to the work you need a server to do.
yabs.mechanism: YABS performs the tests, and the visualizer presents the measurements. It gives you another way to read the output without repeatedly scanning terminal logs.
yabs.payoff: The measurements are easier to work through when you’re comparing servers.
yabs.flowTitle: How to read your YABS results
yabs.evidence: The project has a website you can open and a public repository where you can read the code. Each benchmark describes a particular test, so its conditions matter when comparing results.
yabs.barrier: A benchmark can help you compare machines, but it won’t tell you exactly how your application will run. You still need to consider your own workload.
yabs.demo: Capture real YABS output beside the matching visualization. Highlight the same measurement in both so visitors can trace the source of a displayed value.
yabs.gap: No performance figures, supported import formats or workload wins verified for this rewrite.
alternatives: Compare the measurements behind your VPS choice.
Give YABS output a visual view.

arsenal.headline: Arsenal helps you keep prompts you want to reuse.
arsenal.summary: If you use AI while developing software, some instructions are worth keeping for another task. Arsenal organizes those prompts with their project context so you can return to them.
arsenal.audience: For developers who reuse prompts across their work.
arsenal.experienceTitle: Keep the instructions with their context
arsenal.experience: A prompt makes more sense when you also have the project information it depends on. Arsenal keeps reusable instructions organized around the work they support, so you can adapt them when a similar task comes up.
arsenal.mechanism: Arsenal is a prompt-management project for organizing reusable development instructions and project context.
arsenal.payoff: You have a place to keep instructions that will be useful beyond the current conversation.
arsenal.flowTitle: How you return to a saved prompt
arsenal.evidence: You can open Arsenal through the project link. It focuses on organizing prompts and the development work they support.
arsenal.barrier: You’ll still need to update the context for each task and review what the AI produces. A saved prompt is a starting point for that work.
arsenal.demo: Record saving an actual development prompt and finding it for a second task. Confirm the available controls before scripting the recording.
arsenal.gap: Sharing, search controls, integrations, sync, pricing and workflow execution have not been verified.
alternatives: Keep the instructions that worked.
Give recurring development prompts a home.

scatter.headline: Scatter is a game about dropping a ball through a physics board.
scatter.summary: You drop a ball into the board, watch it bounce through the obstacles and see where it lands. Scatter explores how that simple interaction can be enjoyable on its own.
scatter.audience: For people who enjoy short, playful browser experiments.
scatter.experienceTitle: You follow the ball until it lands
scatter.experience: After you drop a ball, its path changes as it hits the obstacles. You follow those bounces until it reaches the bottom, then you can try another drop.
scatter.mechanism: The game uses a physics simulation to calculate how the ball falls and responds when it hits an obstacle.
scatter.payoff: The enjoyment comes from following the ball and waiting to see where it lands.
scatter.flowTitle: What happens when you drop a ball
scatter.evidence: Scatter is a browser-game experiment. There isn’t a playable build linked on this portfolio yet.
scatter.barrier: This is a game experiment. The portfolio doesn’t offer prizes or payouts.
scatter.demo: Record one uninterrupted ball drop in the actual build, from input to landing, with its real feedback. Show the board rather than a fabricated game screenshot.
scatter.gap: Public build URL and supported devices have not been verified for the portfolio.
alternatives: See where the next bounce takes you.
One drop, a board full of possibilities.

laundirii.headline: LaunDiri connects the people handling a laundry order.
laundirii.summary: A customer places a laundry request, but a courier and a shop also have a part in completing it. LaunDiri is an Android team project exploring how those roles can work together in one application.
laundirii.audience: For people exploring coordination in a laundry service.
laundirii.experienceTitle: The order needs to work for each person involved
laundirii.experience: The customer starts a request, and the courier and shop handle their parts of the service. The project brings those roles into one workflow so the handoffs are part of the design.
laundirii.mechanism: The application connects the customer request with courier and shop participation in the order.
laundirii.payoff: The design accounts for the people who handle the order after the customer places it.
laundirii.flowTitle: How a laundry request moves between people
laundirii.evidence: LaunDiri is a collaborative Android application project focused on laundry coordination.
laundirii.barrier: LaunDiri is presented here as a team project. You can’t book a laundry service through this page, and it doesn’t offer delivery times or service coverage.
laundirii.demo: Capture the same test order from the customer, courier and shop views. Show only handoffs supported by the actual app.
laundirii.gap: Current availability, exact role permissions, order status updates, team contributions and operational rollout need confirmation.
alternatives: One laundry request, more than one person.
Designing the handoffs behind laundry day.

techno-dynamic.headline: Techno Dynamic brings course material and learning questions together.
techno-dynamic.summary: Techno Dynamic is a team project for technopreneurship courses. It combines course material with AI-assisted content and suggestions based on frequently asked questions, giving learners more ways to explore a subject.
techno-dynamic.audience: For learners exploring technopreneurship course material.
techno-dynamic.experienceTitle: Questions can help you explore the lesson further
techno-dynamic.experience: You start with the course material and explore generated content and related suggestions. Those suggestions give you another way to approach a topic you want to understand.
techno-dynamic.mechanism: The platform combines course material, AI-assisted content generation and suggestions based on frequently asked questions.
techno-dynamic.payoff: You can explore related explanations when you want more context for a lesson.
techno-dynamic.flowTitle: How the learning material fits together
techno-dynamic.evidence: The project explores generated content and question-based suggestions for learning. There isn’t a study here showing that it improves learning outcomes.
techno-dynamic.barrier: Generated explanations need checking against reliable course material. They can support further exploration, but their accuracy shouldn’t be assumed.
techno-dynamic.demo: Record a real course section with its associated FAQ suggestion and resulting content. Use a verified lesson and retain any review notices.
techno-dynamic.gap: Live access, sources used for generation, educator review and specific team contributions need confirmation.
alternatives: A course page with somewhere to take your questions.
Bring technopreneurship material and questions together.

rad-ai.headline: Rad AI shows the output of an ultrasound classification experiment.
rad-ai.summary: Rad AI connects an ultrasound research image to a classification model and displays the result. It’s a research prototype for inspecting model output, and it must not be used for diagnosis.
rad-ai.experienceTitle: Follow the image through the experiment
rad-ai.experience: You provide a suitable research image, run it through the classifier and inspect the result it returns. The interface makes that experimental process easier to follow.
rad-ai.mechanism: The interface passes the image to a machine-learning model and displays its classification output.
rad-ai.payoff: You can inspect the model’s response to an image through an interface.
rad-ai.flowTitle: How an image becomes a model result
rad-ai.evidence: Rad AI is documented as an ultrasound-classification prototype. No clinical validation or accuracy figures are supplied here.
rad-ai.barrier: The prototype hasn’t been validated as a medical device. It must not be used to diagnose someone or make clinical decisions.
rad-ai.demo: Use an authorized non-identifying research image and capture its actual model output. Keep the research-only notice visible. Do not invent confidence values.
rad-ai.gap: Model metrics, datasets, evaluation method, current availability and clinical validity are unverified.
alternatives: From an ultrasound image to an experimental prediction.
Put a classification experiment where it can be inspected.

jungle-guardians.headline: Jungle Guardians lets you explore how a model classifies animal images.
jungle-guardians.summary: You choose an animal image, run it through a classifier and look at the category it predicts. Jungle Guardians uses that process to make image classification easier to explore.
jungle-guardians.audience: For learners exploring computer vision with animal images.
jungle-guardians.experienceTitle: Compare the predicted category with the image
jungle-guardians.experience: After the model returns a category, you can compare it with the animal in the picture. That gives you a way to think about both the prediction and the mistakes the model might make.
jungle-guardians.mechanism: The interface sends an animal image to a classification model and shows its predicted category.
jungle-guardians.payoff: You can explore a model’s behavior using images you can also interpret yourself.
jungle-guardians.flowTitle: How an animal image is classified
jungle-guardians.evidence: Jungle Guardians is an interactive image-classification learning project. No accuracy benchmark is supplied here.
jungle-guardians.barrier: A predicted category can be wrong. This page doesn’t establish which species the model can identify reliably.
jungle-guardians.demo: Record a permitted animal image and the actual returned category. Include a real failure case if available, without inventing predictions.
jungle-guardians.gap: Supported categories, training data, evaluation and public access require verification.
alternatives: See what a model makes of an animal photo.
Explore animal classification one image at a time.

contact-manager.headline: Contact Manager gives you a place to manage contact records.
contact-manager.summary: Contact Manager is an application project for browsing contact records and maintaining the details stored in them. It focuses on the information you need to return to when you want to reach someone.
contact-manager.audience: For people maintaining a collection of contact records.
contact-manager.experienceTitle: Find a contact and maintain their details
contact-manager.experience: You can browse the stored records, work with their information and return to a contact when you need the details again.
contact-manager.mechanism: The project uses Angular for the interface and Supabase for the data side of the application.
contact-manager.payoff: The contact information is organized in a dedicated application.
contact-manager.flowTitle: How you work with contact records
contact-manager.evidence: Contact Manager is documented as an Angular and Supabase application project. No security or scale assessment is supplied here.
contact-manager.barrier: The project description doesn’t establish whether the application is suitable for sensitive customer information. That would need a separate assessment.
contact-manager.demo: Use fictional contact details in an actual build. Show browsing a record and a supported edit, then confirm the saved value before presenting that capability.
contact-manager.gap: Authentication, data access policies, supported edit operations, import/export and live availability need verification.
alternatives: Return to the contact record you need.
Give contact records a focused workspace.

affiliatour.headline: Affiliatour helps you make product videos without repeating every edit.
affiliatour.summary: I’m a video editor, and making similar product videos by hand takes time. Affiliatour helps you reuse intro hooks and product clips to prepare a batch of videos, then review what you want to post.
affiliatour.audience: For creators preparing short product videos.
affiliatour.experienceTitle: Keep the structure and change the clips
affiliatour.experience: The format I’m working with starts with a short introduction, followed by several shots of the product. If you already have that footage, you can reuse the structure instead of assembling every version from the beginning.
affiliatour.mechanism: Import your intro hooks and product clips, organize them by project and adjust the timing. Affiliatour renders a batch on your device so you can review the videos before posting them.
affiliatour.payoff: You can spend less of the editing session repeating the same assembly work.
affiliatour.flowTitle: Build several videos from a repeatable format
affiliatour.evidence: The App Store listing describes batches of up to 100 short videos and on-device preparation, rendering and review.
affiliatour.barrier: Review each video before posting. Producing more videos doesn’t guarantee search visibility, audience growth or sales.
affiliatour.demo: Use the official App Store listing and app icon.
affiliatour.gap: Capabilities summarized from Apple lookup API for app 6769322267, Philippines storefront. End-to-end rendering was not tested in this portfolio task.
alternatives: Turn your product clips into a batch you can review.
Prepare product videos together in Affiliatour.

iconnek.headline: Iconnek is for finding people you have something in common with.
iconnek.summary: I want to build a business, and I’ve found it hard to meet people with similar goals. That’s where Iconnek started: describe who you are and what matters to you, then find people you’d like to talk with.
iconnek.audience: For people looking for conversations around shared interests and goals.
iconnek.experienceTitle: Start with who you are, beyond your job
iconnek.experience: Your industry only tells part of your story. You might have an interest or a goal that has little to do with your work. Iconnek is built around helping those parts of you inform the people you meet.
iconnek.mechanism: The idea is to use AI to bring people into small groups based on what they share about themselves. I also want the matching to learn from conversations and reactions over time; that is part of the direction, not a claim that every part is already available.
iconnek.payoff: The aim is to make it easier to find people you can have a meaningful conversation with.
iconnek.flowTitle: From describing yourself to meeting people
iconnek.evidence: The public landing page explains the project and its focus on shared interests and small groups.
iconnek.barrier: More specific people filters and guided profile questions are planned. Check the current app before relying on a particular matching feature.
iconnek.demo: Use the existing app icon and landing page. Do not simulate live AI matching as proof.
iconnek.gap: Owner notes describe intended AI grouping and future refinement. Conversation/reaction-based matching and advanced filters are not verified as live features.
alternatives: Find people who share the things that matter to you.
Your interests can help you find people to talk with.
